entry.label: Recursion
entry.description: A family of relations in which a definition, operation, organisation or observation is reapplied to instances of the same kind. The domain, recurrence rule and boundary condition must be stated.
entry.canonical_definition: A family of domain-specific relations in which a definition, operation, structure or organisation is reapplied to instances of the same kind. A conforming account must state the domain, recurrence rule and boundary or termination condition; organisational recursion is not automatically computational recursion or visual self-similarity.

profile.title: Recursion
profile.canonical_definition: A family of domain-specific relations in which a definition, operation, structure or organisation is reapplied to instances of the same kind. A conforming account must state the domain, recurrence rule and boundary or termination condition; organisational recursion is not automatically computational recursion or visual self-similarity.
profile.summary: Recursion is a family resemblance across domains, not one universal mechanism. A definition may refer to itself through smaller cases; a computation may call itself; an organisation may contain operational systems with corresponding viability requirements.
profile.why_it_matters: Nested diagrams easily look profound. A sound recursive claim states what recurs, what changes between levels, what the base or boundary condition is and why the same structural relation applies.
historical_lineage: formal recursive definition and recursive-function theory
second-order observation and reflexivity as a distinct neighbouring lineage
logical_antecedents: identity of the operation or structure
rule for moving to another instance or level
domain in which sameness is claimed
practice_connections: show what recurs and what does not
do not infer sameness from visual nesting
common_misreadings: fractal means recursive and vice versa
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.

sources.title: Recursion - Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.notes: NIST technical dictionary entry defining algorithmic recursion as a function calling itself on a part of a task, with base and recursive cases. It defines one domain-specific use, not the whole cross-disciplinary concept.
sources.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology

sources.title: Recursive Functions
sources.notes: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry covering recursive definitions, recursive functions, computability and their history. Useful for separating formal recursion from analogy and later organisational uses.

sources.title: Viable System Model - The VSM in 1000 words
sources.notes: Metaphorum explainer identifying Ashby's requisite variety, Wiener's cybernetics and the mathematics of recursive systems among the VSM's theoretical bases. Used as a public bridge source pending exact primary-book locators.

sources.title: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
sources.notes: Alan Turing's foundational computability paper. It is retained as formal context for recursive-function theory, not treated as the origin of recursion itself.
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society

sources.title: Diagnosing the System for Organizations
sources.notes: Stafford Beer's guide to diagnosing organisations with the Viable System Model. The exact primary-book pages for the recursive-system theorem remain to be located before the organisational-recursion relation is promoted.

sources.title: The Grammar of Systems - SCiO presentation
sources.notes: Lists 33 systems laws and principles and describes nine patterns of thinking.

sources.title: The Grammar of Systems II: From Order to Chaos and Back Again, 2nd edition
sources.notes: Current second-edition metadata. The book presents nine systems-thinking patterns and 33 systems laws and principles.

sources.title: Cybersecurity Lessons from The Grammar of Systems, part 3
sources.notes: Public secondary summary of Grammar of Systems items 23–33. Used as an accessible orientation aid; the book remains the controlling source.
